paperBird.purpose: Canonical original official project mascot: README, landing page, and Starlight header. Favicon identity derives from this same bird.
paperBird.invariant: Preserve original bytes and full transparent canvas. Proportional display sizing only; no simplification, cropping, trimming, or redrawing.

favicon.generation: image_gen edit of the approved original bird.
favicon.usage: Landing declares 16px, 32px, and 48px exports; Starlight uses 48px.
favicon.invariant: Only small-size framing and contour cleanup of the same complete bird; preserve pose, colors, wing, eye, beak, and feet. Original mascot is unchanged.

officialShare.purpose: Selected white publishing-poster default official-site link preview.
officialShare.invariant: Typography, artwork, and layout generated together with the approved bird reference in one image_gen call per candidate. Only proportional resize and lossless PNG encoding afterward; the selected white asset remains byte-identical.
officialShare.alternate: Dark alternate adds an approved warm-cream oval paper disk behind the feet through a localized image_gen edit; white publishing cover stays selected.
officialShare.alternatePostprocessing: Proportional resize and lossless PNG encoding only; no manual compositing, cropping, relettering, or further layout changes.

brandAssets.scope: Official project identity extension. Existing UI palette and type remain fixed; generated explorers and custom themes retain independent assets and metadata.

narrative.overview:
Dirwell uses the visual language of a maintained technical catalog: warm paper, precise rules, readable metadata, and a restrained deployment blue. The official site is editorial at the top and increasingly dense as it explains the product. The generated explorer remains a separate, compact inventory interface that third-party themes may replace without inheriting the official site's tokens.

The approved folded-paper bird is the official project identity. Its cream page-body, large observant eye, orange-red folded wing, and curious pose add a recognizable character to the catalog. The original illustration anchors the README, landing page, and documentation header; a minimal adaptation of the same bird supplies the favicon. Complete editorial share artwork extends it to link previews. This extension preserves the incumbent palette, typography, and layout.
keyCharacteristics: Editorial display type leads; interface type carries actions and metadata.
The paper bird identifies the project; real terminal and file-ledger content prove its behavior.
Thin rules organize dense information; rounded surfaces are reserved for controls and demonstrations.
Keyboard focus and reduced-motion behavior are part of the visual system.

rules.name: The Deployment Blue Rule
rules.body: Use the accent to show navigation or action, never as a large decorative field.

rules.name: The Ledger Type Rule
rules.body: Use tabular numerals for file sizes, dates, and other aligned measurements.

rules.name: The Evidence Surface Rule
rules.body: Elevation identifies a working example or code artifact, not a generic content container.

dos: Do show real commands, directory entries, and build modes when explaining capability.
Do keep examples paired with both their live output and source directory.
Do lead with product value and a working preview, then first commands, examples, and advanced options.
Do keep focus visible and motion optional.
Do reuse the original paper-bird PNG and preserve proportional display sizing.
donts: Don't replace the favicon with a different character, unrelated badge, or cropped bird body.
Don't derive new UI palette colors from the illustration or force official-site branding into explorer themes.
Don't crop, manually composite, or reletter generated share artwork; the approved dark-cover disk is a localized image-tool edit.
Don't turn the page into an equal-card feature grid.
Don't use invented adoption claims, customers, metrics, or testimonials.
Don't use Unicode arrows or emoji as interface icons.
Don't force third-party themes to inherit either the official-site or default-theme palette.
